name_ar: تصميم الأيقونات بالتشابه والإغلاق البصري
name_en: Icon design by resemblance and Gestalt closure
what: يصمم أيقونات تشبه ما تمثله أو تعتمد على إكمال العين للشكل الناقص، ويعرف متى يفشل التبسيط. — Designs icons that look like what they mean or let the eye complete a partial outline, and knows when simplification fails.
when: تصميم أيقونة، أيقونات واضحة، شعار بمساحة سلبية / icon design, negative-space logo, partial-outline icon
how: 1) Use resemblance when the object has a stable, widely known look (camera, lock, folder); switch to a convention icon when the thing is abstract. 2) Distinguish near neighbours by one decisive feature (camera vs video: add the record dot or a film frame). 3) Closure: suggest the shape with a partial outline or negative space; the viewer completes it, which lowers visual weight. 4) Do not rely on closure when completion costs the user effort in high-stakes UI, or when the icon becomes so reduced it is ambiguous. 5) Test at the smallest real size and with people who have not seen the brief.

name_ar: مقاييس الوضوح والقراءة: التباين والتباعد وطول السطر
name_en: Legibility and readability numbers: contrast, spacing, measure
what: يضبط تباين النص وتباعد الحروف والأسطر وطول السطر بقيم مرجعية قابلة للقياس. — Sets text contrast, tracking, leading and line length to measurable reference values.
when: النص غير مقروء، تباين، حجم الخط، تباعد الأسطر / text hard to read, contrast ratio, line height
how: 1) Contrast: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text (18pt or 14pt bold) and UI graphics, 7:1 for AAA or poor viewing; check with a contrast tool or axe/Lighthouse. 2) Measure: 45-75 characters per line for prose, about 66 ideal. 3) Leading: headings 1.1-1.3, body 1.5-1.7, UI labels 1.2-1.4. 4) Loosen tracking slightly on ALL-CAPS and small text, tighten large display type; avoid long all-caps navigation. 5) Paragraph spacing large enough to see chunks. 6) Legibility (each glyph) is not readability (sustained reading): a display face may pass one and fail the other.

name_ar: التدرج الطباعي بسلم مقاسات
name_en: Typographic hierarchy from a modular type scale
what: يبني تسلسل العناوين والنص من سلم نسب ثابت ووزن الخط بدلاً من أحجام عشوائية. — Builds heading and body ranks from a fixed ratio scale plus weight instead of arbitrary sizes.
when: عناوين غير واضحة، سلم خطوط، أحجام الخط / type scale, heading hierarchy, font sizes
how: 1) Pick one ratio for the product: 1.125 dense app UI, 1.2 gentle software UI, 1.25 general web default, 1.333 editorial, 1.414 print, 1.5 magazine, 1.618 hero/marketing. 2) Generate tokens display, h1-h4, body-lg, body, body-sm, caption, micro from it. 3) Use weight as the second axis and combine it with size (24px semibold reads higher than 24px regular). 4) In monochrome or one-colour palettes, hierarchy must come from size, weight and space alone. 5) Review: each rank must be distinguishable at a glance from its neighbours.

name_ar: الأنماط الأصلية للعلامة والشخصية والتميمة
name_en: Brand archetypes for voice, mascot and character design
what: يختار نمطاً أصلياً واحداً من اثني عشر (الحكيم، المستكشف، المهرّج…) ليوجّه صوت العلامة وتصميم الشخصية أو التميمة. — Chooses one of twelve archetypes (Sage, Explorer, Jester...) to steer brand voice and mascot or character design.
when: تصميم شخصية للعلامة، تميمة، ماسكوت، هوية / mascot design, brand character, brand personality
how: 1) Name the core motivation first, then map to one archetype: Innocent (safety), Sage (truth), Explorer (freedom), Outlaw (disruption), Magician (transformation), Hero (mastery), Lover (intimacy), Jester (joy), Everyman (belonging), Caregiver, Creator, Ruler. 2) Derive shape language, colour, posture and voice from that motivation (Jester: round forms, bright accents, playful copy). 3) Keep one primary archetype, at most one secondary. 4) Test across cultures: reactions to archetypes vary, so validate with the actual audience.

name_ar: رسم أيقونة التطبيق بالكود
name_en: App icon drawn in code as flat layers
what: يرسم أيقونة التطبيق من 1-4 أشكال بسيطة بالكود، طبقة لكل شكل، ثم يقارنها بأيقونات النظام بكل المقاسات. — Draws the app icon from 1-4 simple shapes in code, one layer per shape, then previews it beside system icons at every size.
when: أيقونة تطبيق، app icon، رسم أيقونة بالكود / app icon, draw icon in code, macOS icon
how: 1) Say what the app is in one object or scene users recognise. 2) Sketch it as 1-4 shapes on a grid; each shape becomes its own layer. 3) Choose a background gradient and 3-5 accents; dark or saturated fills make light shapes pop. 4) Canvas 1024x1024, keep the artwork in the middle ~60% (at ~78% it looks oversized), draw flat (solid or gentle two-stop gradient) and let the platform add the material. 5) Avoid motifs that read as the platform's own apps. 6) Render previews from 256 down to 16 pt beside system icons before shipping.

name_ar: تصميم واجهة غير قالبي وملف DESIGN.md
name_en: Anti-template interface design and a DESIGN.md north star
what: يتجنب الأشكال الافتراضية المكررة للواجهات، ويكتب ملف تصميم واحد واضح الرأي بالألوان والخطوط والتخطيط يرجع إليه البشر والنماذج. — Avoids the stock look of generated interfaces and writes one opinionated design file (palette, type, layout, principles) that people and models follow.
when: تصميم موقع مميز، واجهة ليست مكررة، دليل تصميم / distinctive UI, design guide, avoid generic look
how: 1) Ground the design in the subject matter, not a template. 2) List and avoid default looks: cream + serif + terracotta, near-black + one acid accent, broadsheet hairlines, identical rounded SaaS cards with the same grey shadow, tracked ALL-CAPS eyebrows above every heading, meta strings joined by middle dots. 3) Plan, review against the brief, build, critique: palette as 4-6 named hex values, typefaces and roles, a layout concept compared in ASCII wireframes, then principles. 4) Capture it in DESIGN.md with a theme or north star, the why behind each rule and concrete tokens; hedging guides are ignored.

name_ar: التفاعلات الدقيقة: المحفّز والقواعد والاستجابة والحلقات
name_en: Microinteractions: trigger, rules, feedback, loops and modes
what: يصمم التفاصيل الصغيرة للأزرار والمفاتيح والتحميل ويقيّمها بثمانية بنود. — Designs the small details of toggles, buttons and loaders and scores them on eight rows.
when: تفاعل زر، حركة صغيرة في الواجهة، micro interaction / microinteraction, button feedback, toggle animation
how: 1) Trigger: shows that it exists, what it does and its state; prominence matches stakes; gestures get a visible alternative; default/hover/active/disabled/loading states look different. 2) Rules: simple and predictable, constrain inputs instead of erroring. 3) Feedback under 100 ms, scaled to the event's importance (not uniform). 4) Loops and modes: define what repeats or expires, avoid hidden modes. 5) Score 9-10 when all eight rows pass, 5-6 for generic feel, ≤3 when feedback or triggers are missing.

name_ar: شرح بصري بصيغة واحدة مناسبة للسؤال
name_en: Visual explanation: one format chosen by the question
what: يجيب عن «وضّح لي» برسم واحد مناسب (شجرة استدعاء، مخطط Mermaid، فرق كود…) مبني فقط على ما ثبت. — Answers 'show me' with one fitting visual (call tree, Mermaid diagram, focused diff...) built only from verified facts.
when: وضّح بالرسم، ارسم لي مخطط، اشرح بصرياً / show me, sketch it, visualize this flow
how: 1) Name the question the visual must answer. 2) Pick one format: pseudocode for logic and state transitions; indented call tree for runtime flow; shallow tree for ownership; Mermaid for actors and data flow; focused diff for a proposed change; HTML only when asked or previewable. 3) Extract only verified calls, files, states and actors. 4) One labelled visual next to the sentence it supports, plus one or two sentences of explanation. 5) Mark unknowns as unknown, never fill gaps with plausible architecture.

name_ar: الإفصاح التدريجي للمعلومات والأدوات
name_en: Progressive disclosure of information and controls
what: يقسّم الواجهة أو الشرح إلى طبقات: ما يلزم للقرار الحالي أولاً، والباقي خلف خطوة واحدة. — Layers an interface or explanation: what the current decision needs first, the rest one step away.
when: واجهة مزدحمة، إخفاء الخيارات المتقدمة / cluttered UI, advanced options, layered help
how: 1) Every visible element costs noticing, reading and evaluating. 2) Sort options by frequency and relevance; show the primary layer, tuck advanced ones behind one clear disclosure (expand, 'more', a second step). 3) Make the hidden layer discoverable and its trigger explicit. 4) Do not hide what most users need often, and do not nest more than two levels. 5) Same rule applies to documents and skills: summary first, references one level deep.
